0d2cd399b9a119a03b600e3c906bec535f03641b.summary: Both passages give the same rule on abstraction: don't extract speculative or superficial abstractions, but do extract a concrete, domain-owned one when real shared behavior or duplication justifies it.

passages.text:
- Do not abstract two things merely because they look similar. First establish
  that they have the same behavior, ownership, change reason, and invariants.
  A small amount of local duplication is preferable to a premature generic
  abstraction that couples unrelated callers.
- Refactor repeated behavior when the shared rule is real and the abstraction
  makes both callers clearer. Keep the abstraction close to the domain that
  owns it; avoid a generic utility module becoming a dumping ground.

- Do not introduce speculative abstractions or abstractions solely because a
  change might be reusable. A concrete, domain-owned abstraction that
  improves cohesion, removes real duplication, or makes a branch independently
  testable is not premature; use it when the code evidence supports it, even
  when the task did not name the extraction. Keep it as small as possible.

1864129a77cdc6a3b95f9fa70bb0ec59cbd977b7.summary: Both passages instruct testing observable behavior/contracts rather than private implementation details, so a behavior-preserving refactor shouldn't force test rewrites.

passages.text:
- Test observable behavior and public contracts, not private implementation
  details. A refactor that preserves the contract should not require rewriting
  the tests.

- Add or update tests with behavior changes. Test observable behavior and
  important failure modes, not private implementation details. A test is
  useful only when it can fail for a real regression.

2862790b65abcc585b82de2f8744d060b97c4610.summary: Both passages tell the agent to avoid adding new dependencies and prefer what already exists (standard library, existing packages) unless a new dependency is genuinely justified.

passages.text:
- Prefer the standard library and existing project dependencies before adding
  a new package. Keep dependency additions justified by a real capability or
  maintenance benefit, not by a shorter one-off expression.
- No new dependency if it can be avoided.

7e45f4104af8df999f7b0fe5e3c723fde92eb2d5.summary: Both passages require running the project's formatter, static checks, and tests before handing off a change, and forbid claiming checks passed without actually running them.

passages.text:
- Before handing off a change, run the project's formatter, linter, type
  checker, and relevant tests. When no project-specific commands exist, a
  reasonable baseline is `python -m compileall`, the configured test command,
  and the configured static checks; do not claim checks passed without running
  them.
